config.title: House Robber II

intro.title: House Robber II
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a solution to the House Robber II lesson, where you need to maximize the amount of money a robber can steal from houses arranged in a circle without triggering adjacent alarms. You'll learn how to apply dynamic programming concepts to break down this circular lesson into two linear subproblems. The implementation will involve using JavaScript arrays, loops, and helper functions to calculate optimal results. By the end, you'll understand how to handle circular constraints by solving simpler linear cases and combining their results.
intro.usecase: The House Robber II algorithm pattern appears in resource allocation systems where you need to maximize value while respecting constraints on adjacent selections. In finance dashboards, this helps optimize investment portfolios by selecting non-adjacent high-yield assets while avoiding risk clusters. E-commerce platforms use similar logic for dynamic pricing engines to maximize revenue without discounting adjacent product categories. This circular constraint pattern also appears in scheduling systems for optimizing shift assignments or equipment maintenance rotations in manufacturing interfaces.

objectives: Apply the dynamic programming approach to solve the House Robber II lesson
Construct a helper function to handle the linear House Robber subproblem
Initialize and manipulate two separate DP arrays for circular constraint scenarios
Integrate boundary condition checks for circular neighborhood constraints
Implement the main solution function that orchestrates both circular cases
Configure base cases for single-house and two-house scenarios
Control state transitions in the DP tables to track maximum robbery amounts
